summary: Deserialization in JDBC user and role services allows administrator code execution
description:
The JDBC user group and role services read user and role property values with `ResultSet.getObject()`. An
administrator could configure a service backed by an uploaded HSQLDB database whose property values are serialized
Java objects. These were deserialized when users or roles were loaded, executing code.

This was reported as step 5 of an unauthenticated remote command execution chain, see
[GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq).

### Impact

An administrator, or anyone who takes over an administrator session, can execute code with the operating system
privileges of the GeoServer process.

### Details

`JDBCUserGroupService` and `JDBCRoleService` read the property value column with `getObject()`. For an HSQLDB
`OTHER` column the driver deserializes the value with an unrestricted `ObjectInputStream`. The JDBC security module
and HSQLDB driver are part of the standard distribution, and the REST API allows an administrator to upload a
database file to the data directory and create a JDBC user group service that uses it.

### Mitigation

Limit administrator access to trusted users, and restrict access to the REST API `/rest/resource` and
`/rest/security` endpoints to trusted networks.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

User and role property values are now read as text. No manual steps required.

### References

* [GEOS-12239](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12239)
* [GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq)

summary: WFS stored query exception discloses data directory path
description:
A WFS stored query request with an overlong id returned an exception report containing the absolute data directory
path.

This was reported as step 1 of an unauthenticated remote command execution chain, see
[GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq).

### Impact

An unauthenticated user learns the absolute data directory path. This is not harmful by itself, but other attacks
need it, for example to build `file:` references to data directory files.

### Details

The stored query id is mapped to a file name in the data directory. An id longer than the file system name limit
failed with a file system error, and the WFS exception report included the error message with the full path.

### Mitigation

None needed beyond upgrading; the path alone gives no access.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

Overlong stored query ids are rejected with a short error, and file system errors are logged instead of returned to
the client. No manual steps required.

### References

* [GEOS-12240](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12240)
* [GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq)

cwes.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

summary: Stored XSS via style name in style editor Layer Preview
description:
The web administration style editor renders the style name into inline JavaScript when the "Layer Preview" tab is
selected. The style name was not escaped, so a style whose name contains JavaScript executed that JavaScript in the
browser of the administrator viewing it. This is part of core GeoServer and present on every installation.

### Impact

A user able to create or edit styles, such as a workspace administrator, can plant a style name that runs JavaScript
in an administrator session when an administrator opens that style in the style editor and selects "Layer Preview",
allowing session hijack or any administrative action.

Where styles can be created without an account, as in GHSA-65mr-5frw-93xf (OGC API Styles), no account is needed.

### Details

The style editor Layer Preview builds its OpenLayers script from a FreeMarker template (`ol-load.ftl`) with
auto-escaping off, and the style name was placed inside a JavaScript string literal as is.

### Mitigation

Only allow trusted users to create or edit styles, and check style names for unexpected characters before opening
"Layer Preview".

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

The style editor now escapes values placed in the Layer Preview script. No manual steps required.

### References

* [GEOS-12237](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12237)
* [GHSA-65mr-5frw-93xf](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-65mr-5frw-93xf) unauthenticated style management in OGC API Styles

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

summary: Local file probing via file:// schemaLocation during strict schema validation
description:
An unauthenticated client can set `xsi:schemaLocation` to a `file://` URI in a request to any OWS operation that validates XML against its schema. The schema validation did not use the entity resolver that blocks local file access, so GeoServer opened the local path and returned different errors depending on whether the file exists and whether it is well-formed XML.

### Impact

The differing error responses act as a file system probing oracle: an attacker can learn whether a local file exists and whether it is XML. File contents are not disclosed.

Operations that validate requests include WFS with `strict=true`, WCS 1.0 and 1.1.1, CSW, WPS, and WMS GetMap with `validateSchema=true`.

### Details

The flaw is in GeoTools XML schema validation, see [GHSA-mgjv-wp78-ccrq](https://github.com/geotools/geotools/security/advisories/GHSA-mgjv-wp78-ccrq). The entity resolver configured by GeoServer (`AllowListEntityResolver` by default, or `PreventLocalEntityResolver` when `ENTITY_RESOLUTION_ALLOWLIST=*`) was not applied to the top level schema location during strict parsing.

### Mitigation

Avoid the schema validation code paths where possible, for example leave WFS `strict` disabled, and do not enable WMS `validateSchema`. Restrict access to OWS services that cannot be configured this way (WCS, CSW, WPS) to trusted users.

### Resolution

Upgrade to a GeoServer release that includes GeoTools 33.7, 34.6 or 35.2:

* GeoServer 2.27.7, 2.28.6, 3.0.2

### References

* https://github.com/geotools/geotools/security/advisories/GHSA-mgjv-wp78-ccrq
* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOT-7975

cwes.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

summary: Service security rules bypassed with a prefixed service name such as x/WFS
description:
A `service` parameter with a prefix, such as `service=x/WFS`, was resolved to the WFS service by the dispatcher, but
service security checked the unresolved name `x/WFS`. No rule matched, so operations restricted in service security
ran without a role check. The default configuration restricts `CreateStoredQuery` and `DropStoredQuery` to
administrators, so anonymous users could create and delete WFS stored queries.

This was also reported as step 2 of a remote command execution chain, see
[GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq).

### Impact

An unauthenticated user can call any OWS operation that is restricted only by service security rules
(**Security > Services**, `security/services.properties`). With the default rules this allows creating and deleting
WFS stored queries. Installations that restrict other operations this way, for example WFS `Transaction`, lose that
protection as well. Layer and data security rules still apply.

Stored queries created this way are the entry point for
[GHSA-39mw-5chv-jh47](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-39mw-5chv-jh47).

### Details

`Dispatcher.findService` strips everything up to `/` from the service id to choose the service, while
`OperationSecurityCallback` matched rules against the `service` value of the request, which still held `x/WFS`.

### Mitigation

Block requests whose `service` parameter contains `/`, in the query string or in the `service` attribute of an XML
request, at a proxy in front of GeoServer.

Review the data directory `wfs/query` and `workspaces/*/wfs/query` folders for stored queries you did not create.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

The dispatcher now sets the request service to the resolved service id, so service security checks the service
that runs. No manual steps required.

### References

* [GEOS-12195](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12195)
* [GHSA-39mw-5chv-jh47](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-39mw-5chv-jh47)
* [GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq)
* [Service security](https://docs.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/security/service/)

summary: Unauthenticated WFS GetFeatureById XML injection
description:
GeoServer exposes the built-in WFS 2.0 stored query `urn:ogc:def:query:OGC-WFS::GetFeatureById` through the public `GetFeature` operation. The stored query substituted the caller's `ID` parameter into an XML template without escaping, then parsed the result without GeoServer's entity resolver. An unauthenticated caller could inject XML, including an `xi:include`, into the query.

### Impact

A single unauthenticated WFS request can:

* read a local text file readable by the GeoServer process;
* fetch an attacker selected HTTP or HTTPS URL (server-side request forgery);
* receive the fetched text in the `Illegal property name` error response.

No authentication, custom stored query or `CreateStoredQuery` access is required. Contents are echoed when a layer is published to anonymous users; otherwise the file is still read but not returned.

### Details

`StoredQuery.compile()` replaced the `${ID}` token in the `GetFeatureById` template (`<fes:ResourceId rid='${ID}'/>`) using plain string replacement, so quotes and angle brackets in the value could close the `rid` attribute and add new FES elements. The result was parsed with `new Parser(new WFSConfiguration())` without the catalog entity resolver used elsewhere in the class, so XInclude and external entities were resolved with ordinary URI access.

### Mitigation

Restrict or disable the WFS service for anonymous users using service security, or disable WFS if it is not required.

### Resolution

Stored query parsing now uses the GeoServer entity resolver, and the GeoTools `PreventLocalEntityResolver` checks redirects.

* GeoServer 2.27.7, 2.28.6, 3.0.2
* GeoTools 33.7, 34.6, 35.2

### References

* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12199
* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOT-7938
* https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/9928
* https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-hgm3-wq4h-8vvq
* https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-rv5g-g2r9-58rj

cwes.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

summary: Unauthenticated style management in OGC API Styles
description:
The OGC API Styles community module provides create, update and delete operations for styles. These operations were
available without any authorization, so an unauthenticated user could add a new style, overwrite any global style,
or remove any global style, including styles used by published layers. The equivalent REST API operations
(`/rest/styles`) are restricted to administrators.

### Impact

When the OGC API Styles module is installed, an anonymous attacker can create, replace or delete styles, changing or
breaking the rendering of published layers.

A planted style name could also be used to reach the stored XSS in the style editor, [GHSA-3xvw-cfcr-v3h7](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-3xvw-cfcr-v3h7), without
an account.

### Details

Requests to `/ogc/styles/v1` fall under the default security filter chain, which allows anonymous access, and the
default `services.properties` has no `styles` rules. The `addStyle`, `updateStyle`, `deleteStyle`,
`updateStyleMetadata` and `patchStyleMetadata` handlers wrote to the catalog without any further access check.

### Mitigation

Restrict OGC API Styles write operations to administrators by adding service security rules, in
**Security > Services** or `security/services.properties` in the data directory:

```
styles.addStyle=ROLE_ADMINISTRATOR
styles.updateStyle=ROLE_ADMINISTRATOR
styles.deleteStyle=ROLE_ADMINISTRATOR
styles.updateStyleMetadata=ROLE_ADMINISTRATOR
styles.patchStyleMetadata=ROLE_ADMINISTRATOR
```

Alternatively remove the OGC API Styles community module.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

OGC API Styles management (create, update, delete) is now disabled by default. To use it, enable the
"Manage styles" conformance class (GeoServer 3.0.2: **Services > Styles** page; GeoServer 2.28.6 and 2.27.7:
set `OGCAPI_STYLES_MANAGE=true`), and add the service security rules shown under Mitigation so only
administrators can manage styles.

### References

* [GEOS-12236](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12236)
* [OGC API - Styles](https://docs.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/community/ogc-api/styles/index.html)
* [GHSA-3xvw-cfcr-v3h7](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-3xvw-cfcr-v3h7) stored XSS in the style editor

summary: Predictable remember-me key allows administrator session forgery
description:
The remember-me cookie is signed with a key, together with the user name, expiry and stored password digest. This key
was read from `security/config.xml` in the data directory, and the release data directory ships with the key
`geoserver`, which most installations never change. Anyone who knows the key and an administrator password digest,
for example from a file disclosure, could create a remember-me cookie that GeoServer accepts as an administrator
login, without knowing the password.

This was reported as step 4 of an unauthenticated remote command execution chain. At the request of the CVE Numbering Authority each step of the chain is fixed separately, released in GeoServer 3.0.2:

1. [CVE-2026-129244](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-4v26-c537-jvxc): WFS stored query exception discloses data directory path 
2. [CVE-2026-129243](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-rv5g-g2r9-58rj): Service security rules bypassed with a prefixed service name such as x/WFS
3. [CVE-2026-120705](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-39mw-5chv-jh47): Unauthenticated WFS GetFeatureById XML injection
4. CVE-2026-129245: Predictable remember-me key allows administrator session forgery
5. [CVE-2026-129242](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-9wf2-fcgq-vxhq): Deserialization in JDBC user and role services allows administrator code execution

### Impact

An attacker who obtains an administrator password digest, through any file disclosure or a copy of the data
directory, can log in as that administrator. Changing the key in `security/config.xml` does not help when the same
file disclosure also reveals the key.

### Details

`GeoServerTokenBasedRememberMeServices` validates the cookie signature with the key from the `rememberMeService`
section of `security/config.xml`. The signature uses the stored password digest, not the password, so the digest
and key are enough to forge a cookie.

### Mitigation

Remove `rememberme` from the web filter chain (**Security > Authentication**, filter chain `web`).

Otherwise change the key in `security/config.xml` to a long random value, and protect the data directory from
disclosure.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

The remember-me key is no longer stored in the data directory: each node uses a random key, existing remember-me
cookies are invalidated on upgrade, and a cluster sets a shared key with the `GEOSERVER_REMEMBERME_KEY` application
property.

If you suspect exposure, change administrator passwords.

### References

* [#10008](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/10008)
* [Remember me](https://docs.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/security/webadmin/auth/#remember-me)

summary: Unauthenticated SSRF via WPS gs:DownloadMap (wps-download extension)
description:
GeoServer's `wps-download` extension provides the `gs:DownloadMap` and `gs:DownloadAnimation` processes, used to build a composite map image from a list of layers. Layers can reference the local WMS, or a remote WMS server by giving the process a `Capabilities` URL. The `Capabilities` URL was fetched directly, with no restriction enforced.

### Impact

With the `wps` and `wps-download` extensions installed, anyone who can access the WPS endpoint can issue outbound requests to any address reachable by GeoServer, including internal-only infrastructure that was never meant to be exposed.

This can be used to:

* Scan the internal network to gain insight for further exploits
* Access internal WMS services

### Details

`DownloadMapProcess.getServer()` fetched the caller supplied `Capabilities` URL without consulting URL Checks. The process is available to anonymous users unless WPS process security restricts it.

### Mitigation

Use the WPS process security settings to disable `gs:DownloadMap` and `gs:DownloadAnimation`, or restrict them to trusted roles:

* [Setting access roles](https://docs.geoserver.org/3.0.x/en/user/services/wps/security/#setting-access-roles)

### Resolution

The `Capabilities` URL is subject to URL Checks in GeoServer 2.27.7, 2.28.6 and 3.0.2.

Use URL Checks to allow access to trusted WMS service locations:

* [URL Checks](https://docs.geoserver.org/3.0.x/en/user/security/urlchecks/)

### References

* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12160
* https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/9755

summary: Unauthenticated PostGIS SQL injection in the jsonArrayContains filter function
description:
## Summary

GeoServer is impacted by GeoTools vulnerability CVE-2026-76904 affecting layers published using PostgreSQL 12 or greater which contain a String or JSON field.  The implementation of OGC Filter function `jsonArrayContains(<property>, '<jsonpath>', '<value>')`  writes `<value>` into generated SQL without escaping. The use of OGC Filter is supported directly by WFS `GetFeature` or WMS `GetMap` using the `CQL_FILTER` (or XML `<fes:Filter>`) parameters.

## Impact

SQL Injection vulnerabilities can lead to the execution of arbitrary SQL expressions in the database.

To limit the impact of SQL Injection vulnerabilities it is good practice to configure PostGIS connection pool with limited access rights.  Special attention should be taken to avoid grants to `pg_read_file` (such as `superuser` account `postgres/postgres` in default PostGIS images) which would allow SQL Injection to be turned into a Remote Code Execution.

## Patches

This is addressed by GEOT-7959 as included in the following GeoServer updates:

* GeoServer 3.0.1
* GeoServer 2.28.5
* GeoServer 2.27.6

## References

* https://github.com/geotools/geotools/security/advisories/GHSA-mqjf-5f49-2fjh
* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOT-7959

cwes.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

summary: Unauthenticated SSRF and file read via printing legend icon URL
description:
The GeoServer printing extension (mapfish-print) allowed an unauthenticated print request to supply legend icon URLs that were fetched without checking the `hosts:` allowlist in the print `config.yaml`. This allowed server-side requests to arbitrary hosts and reading local image files with `file://` URLs.

Only print layouts containing a `!legends` block are affected. The default layouts shipped with GeoServer do not include `!legends`.

### Impact

* Server-side request forgery to any URL reachable from the GeoServer host, bypassing the `hosts:` allowlist.
* Local image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, TIFF, BMP) can be embedded in the generated PDF using `file://` URLs. Other files are not returned, but differing errors reveal whether a file exists.
* Requires the printing extension to be installed and a print layout with `!legends`.

### Details

Map layer URLs are validated by `Config.validateUri()` against the `hosts:` allowlist before fetching. The legend renderer (`LegendsBlock`) passed the `icon` values from the print spec `legends` array directly to `PDFUtils.loadImageFromUrl()` without this check. That method accepts plain file paths, `file://`, `data:` and any `http(s)://` URL. Icons containing `image%2Fsvg%2Bxml` were rendered through Batik, which could also fetch resources referenced by the SVG.

### Mitigation

Remove the `!legends` block from the print layouts in `printing/config.yaml`, or remove the printing extension if it is not used.

### Resolution

mapfish-print-v2 now loads legend icon URLs, including SVG icons, through a single method that applies the `hosts:` allowlist.

* GeoServer 2.27.7, 2.28.6, 3.0.2
* mapfish-print-v2 2.3.7, 2.4.2, 2.5.1

### References

* https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print-v2/pull/120
* https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print-v2/pull/121
* https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print-v2/pull/122
* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12274

summary: Unauthenticated SSRF and file read via WPS inline VRT to native GDAL
description:
### Description

The WPS GeoTIFF input decoder wrote inline raster input to a temporary file, and offered it to every registered
raster format to find a reader. When the GDAL extension and native GDAL are installed, this includes GDAL formats,
which identify files by content.

A GDAL virtual raster (VRT) document supplied inline, but declared as `image/tiff`, was therefore opened by native GDAL
during format detection. GDAL processes VRT source references while opening the document, including `/vsicurl/` URLs
and local files.

Inline input contains no URL, so GeoServer URL checks are not applied.

### Impact

An unauthenticated attacker could send a WPS Execute request that causes GeoServer to make HTTP requests to other
servers (SSRF), and read local files accessible to the GeoServer process.

This applies to installations where:
- The WPS extension is installed, and WPS allows anonymous access (the default).
- The GDAL extension is installed, with native GDAL available.

GeoServer installations without native GDAL are not affected.

### Mitigation

Use one of:
* Remove the GDAL extension, or the native GDAL library.
* Restrict WPS to trusted roles with service security.
* Disable the GDAL VRT driver with the environment variable `GDAL_SKIP=VRT`.

GDAL 3.12 and newer restrict raw raster band sources to files next to the VRT by default
(`GDAL_VRT_RAWRASTERBAND_ALLOWED_SOURCE`), which limits the local file read, but not requests to other servers.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

WPS GeoTIFF inputs are now read with the GeoTIFF format only, input that is not a GeoTIFF is rejected.

### References

* [#10004](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/10004)
* [GHSA-xqwh-vc83-cp7g](https://github.com/GeoWebCache/geowebcache/security/advisories/GHSA-xqwh-vc83-cp7g)
* [GDAL security considerations, VRT driver](https://gdal.org/en/stable/user/security.html#gdal-vrt-driver)

cwes.name: External Control of File Name or Path

summary: CSW DirectDownload served for layers where it is disabled
description:
### Description

The CSW extension DirectDownload operation can be disabled globally or per layer. When disabled, the
download link was removed from CSW records, but a DirectDownload request for the layer still worked.

### Impact

A user able to access a file based raster layer can download its original raster files even when the
administrator has disabled DirectDownload for that layer. Layer access security is still enforced.

Only affects installations with the CSW extension installed.

### Mitigation

Use **Service security** to restrict the DirectDownload operation to administrators:

```
csw.DirectDownload=ADMIN
```

Alternatively remove the CSW extension.

### Resolution

Patched for:

* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7 

### References

* [GEOS-12238](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12238)

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: JWT Headers community module roles header trusted without validation
description:
### Description

The JWT Headers community module identifies users and roles from JWT or JSON information in request headers.

When configured with separate user identity and roles headers, the module validated the identity JWT (signature,
expiration and audience), but trusted the roles header without the same validation.

### Impact

A user with a valid low privilege identity JWT could send a forged roles header, including a role mapped to
`ROLE_ADMINISTRATOR`, and obtain GeoServer administrator privileges.

This applies to installations where:
- The JWT Headers community module is installed and enabled.
- The filter validates the identity JWT, and reads roles from a different header.
- A proxy in front of GeoServer does not remove or overwrite the roles header.

The default GeoServer configuration is not affected.

### Mitigation

Configure the JWT Headers filter to read roles from the same header as the validated identity JWT, or from a role
service or user group service.

Alternatively configure the proxy in front of GeoServer to remove or overwrite the roles header, and do not allow
direct access to GeoServer.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

With token validation enabled, roles are now only taken from the validated token, or from a role service or user group
service. A filter saved with a separate roles header keeps authenticating its users, but takes no roles from that header,
and the GeoServer log reports it when the filter is loaded.

If roles are deliberately carried by a separate header that your proxy always removes or overwrites, check
**Trust a roles header that is not the validated token** in the filter configuration.

### References

* [GEOS-12222](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12222)
* [JWT Headers configuration](https://docs.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/community/jwt-headers/configuration/)

summary: GeoFence source IP rules bypass via X-Forwarded-For
description:
### Description

GeoFence is an official GeoServer extension that provides fine-grained access control for layers, services, and
workspaces.

GeoFence supports source-IP-based access control rules, such as allowing only a specific internal address to access a
given layer. However, when processing requests, GeoFence trusted the user-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` header as the
source IP.

### Impact

An unauthenticated attacker could spoof the source IP and bypass GeoFence source-address-based access control to read
protected map layer data.

This applies to installations where:
- GeoServer has the GeoFence extension installed and enabled.
- The administrator uses GeoFence `addressRange` / source-IP rules to protect layers or services.
- GeoServer is directly exposed, or a front-end proxy does not sanitize or overwrite `X-Forwarded-For`.

The issue did not allow data writes, workspace management, or other administrative operations.

### Details

GeoFence uses the request source address as one of the conditions when evaluating access rules.

When a request contained an `X-Forwarded-For` header, GeoFence used the first IP address in that header. Only when the
header was absent did it use the remote address provided by the servlet container. A client could therefore choose the
source address used to match GeoFence rules.

### Mitigation

Configure the proxy in front of GeoServer to overwrite `X-Forwarded-For` with the client address,
and do not allow direct access to GeoServer.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6
* GeoServer 2.27.7

GeoServer now resolves the client address in one place, reading `X-Forwarded-For` only from trusted proxies.
If your proxy runs on another host or container, list it in the `GEOSERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` application property,
otherwise IP rules match the proxy address. A customized `web.xml` needs the new `Remote IP Resolution` filter,
see the upgrade notes.

### References

* [GEOS-12235](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12235)
* [Application properties](https://docs.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/configuration/properties/index.html) (`GEOSERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES`)

summary: ACL Source IP rules bypass via X-Forwarded-For
description:
### Description

The ACL community module provides fine-grained access control for GeoServer, deciding whether a request
is allowed based on users, roles, services, layers, source IP addresses, and other conditions.

The module supports source-IP rules, such as allowing only a specific internal address or subnet to access
a given layer. However, when determining the request source IP, the module prioritized the client-supplied
`X-Forwarded-For` header instead of the actual connection source address observed by the server.

### Details

When a request contained `X-Forwarded-For`, the ACL module took the first IP address from that header as the
`sourceAddress`. Only when the header was absent did it use the remote address provided by the servlet container.
A client could therefore choose the source IP value used to match ACL `addressRange` rules.

### Impact

When GeoServer is directly exposed to external users, or a front-end proxy does not clean or overwrite user-supplied
`X-Forwarded-For`, an attacker could impersonate an allowed internal source IP, bypass ACL rules, and read
protected maps or geospatial data.

This applied to installations where:

- GeoServer has the ACL community module installed and enabled.
- The administrator uses ACL `addressRange` / source-IP rules to protect layers or services.
- GeoServer is directly exposed, or a front-end proxy does not sanitize or overwrite `X-Forwarded-For`.

The issue did not allow data writes, workspace management, or other administrative operations.

### Mitigation

Configure the proxy in front of GeoServer to overwrite `X-Forwarded-For` with the client address,
and do not allow direct access to GeoServer.

### Resolution

Patched for:

* GeoServer 3.0.2
* GeoServer 2.28.6 (GeoServer ACL 2.3.3)
* GeoServer 2.27.7 (GeoServer ACL 2.3.3)

GeoServer now resolves the client address in one place, reading `X-Forwarded-For` only from trusted proxies.
If your proxy runs on another host or container, list it in the `GEOSERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES` application property,
otherwise IP rules match the proxy address. A customized `web.xml` needs the new `Remote IP Resolution` filter,
see the upgrade notes.

### References

* [GEOS-12235](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12235)
* [GHSA-37mm-jp7f-64jp](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-37mm-jp7f-64jp)
* [GEOSERVER_TRUSTED_PROXIES](https://docs.geoserver.org/stable/en/user/configuration/properties/)

summary: Remote Code Execution via SQLite JDBC Extension Loading in GeoServer JDBC Security Configuration
description:
GeoServer's JDBC user/group service, role service and authentication provider accepted an administrator supplied JDBC connection URL and DML/DDL property file paths without validation. Choosing the SQLite driver with the `enable_load_extension=true` connection parameter, together with a DML file containing `SELECT load_extension(...)`, loads a native library of the attacker's choice into the GeoServer process.

### Impact

An administrator, or anyone with access to an administrator session, can execute arbitrary code as the user running GeoServer.

* On Windows both the DML file and the extension library can be loaded from an SMB share (UNC path), so no files need to be staged on the server.
* On other platforms the attacker must first place the DML file and library on the server file system.

### Details

`AbstractJDBCService.initializeDSFromConfig()` passed the configured driver class and connection URL directly to the connection pool. `checkORCreateJDBCPropertyFile()` accepted absolute paths for the DML and DDL property files, including UNC paths. The DML statements run when the service is used, for example when listing users.

### Mitigation

Restrict access to the GeoServer administration console and REST API to trusted administrators, and do not install JDBC drivers that are not required (such as SQLite) on the GeoServer classpath.

### Resolution

JDBC security services now accept only known drivers and connection parameters for each driver, and reject absolute DML/DDL file paths. Additional parameters can be allowed with the `GEOSERVER_JDBC_EXTRA_PARAMETERS` property.

* GeoServer 2.27.7, 2.28.6, 3.0.2

### References

* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-12234
* https://docs.geoserver.org/3.0.x/en/user/configuration/properties/

summary: RCE and secrets exfiltration via pull_request_target
description:
## Summary

The `sonarcloud-fork-pr.yaml` workflow in geoserver/geoserver-cloud repository used a `pull_request_target` trigger with `actions/checkout` referencing `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}`, then executes `./mvnw verify` on the checked-out code.

This provided an opening to execute arbitrary code on the GitHub Actions runner;  with possibility of exfiltrating repository secrets including those with write permissions over the repository.

## Impact

Review showed that:

* Fork PRs: The workflow only ran for fork PRs from known community contributors with ordinary, non-malicious changes. No PR has been observed that would have exfiltrated secrets such as tokens.
* Download Artifacts: GitHub actions are not used to build project download artifacts; these are built on their own build server and uploaded to SourceForge.
* Build Artifacts: Review of  the [osgeo nexus](https://repo.osgeo.org/) showed no new new artifacts being published during the period of vulnerability.

## Remediation

The workflow has been rewritten on both main and release/2.28.x to follow the GitHub Security Lab "Preventing pwn requests" pattern.

* The vulnerable workflow file no longer exists on any branch in the repository, so any in-flight or future fork PR cannot trigger the original vector.
* Coordinate changing of secrets.
* No evidence of supply chain attack during affected time frame

## References

- [GitHub Security Lab: Keeping your GitHub Actions and workflows secure](https://securitylab.github.com/resources/github-actions-preventing-pwn-requests/)
- [GitHub Docs: Security hardening for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver-cloud/pull/843

summary: Unauthenticated XXE file read and SSRF via xsi:schemaLocation in OWS requests
description:
### Description

An unauthenticated OWS request can name an attacker-controlled XML schema in its `xsi:schemaLocation` attribute.
GeoServer fetched that schema to validate imports and includes, and the schema could declare an external DTD whose
nested entities read a local file readable by the GeoServer process. The file contents were sent to an
attacker-controlled server, or returned in the service exception report.

The schema processing is shared by the OWS services, so the same request works through CSW `GetRecords`,
WFS with `strict=true`, WCS 1.1.1, and WCS 1.0.0 `DescribeCoverage`.

Both WFS and WCS are core services, so a default installation is affected.

### Impact

An unauthenticated attacker can read any file readable by the GeoServer process, such as `security/users.xml` in the
data directory, and can make GeoServer send requests to hosts of the attacker's choice (SSRF).

### Details

The parser loads schemas named in `xsi:schemaLocation` through `Schemas.validateImportsIncludes`. Entity resolution
for the nested DTD was not restricted, so parameter entities in the attacker's DTD were expanded. The request is
accepted on any OWS endpoint, so blocking a single service or endpoint does not prevent it.

### Mitigation

There is no configuration workaround, upgrade to a patched release.

Blocking outgoing connections from the GeoServer host prevents the attacker's schema from being fetched.

### Resolution

Patched for:
* GeoServer 3.0.0
* GeoServer 2.28.4
* GeoServer 2.27.6

The fix restricts entity resolution while validating schema imports and includes ([GEOT-7883](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOT-7883), GeoTools 35.0, 34.4 and 33.6). No manual steps required.

### References

* [GEOT-7883](https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOT-7883)
* [GHSA-rg89-jmrw-x26f](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/security/advisories/GHSA-rg89-jmrw-x26f) addresses the remaining first schema fetch, fixed in GeoServer 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7

summary: Arbitrary file write vulnerability in Master Password Dump Page
description:
### Summary
A vulnerability exists that allows an authenticated administrator with access to GeoServer's security system to pass arbitrary file names to the Master Password Dump web page and create files containing the master password in plaintext. The provided file name must be an absolute path to the target file, the target file can not already exist and all parent directories must already exist.

### Details
When dumping the master password, GeoServer will use the provided file name with minimal validation as long as it is a java.io.File path. The only limitation is that the fix for a previous, unrelated vulnerability prevents relative path traversal here but absolute paths can be used to access arbitrary files. GeoServer does not enforce a maximum password length by default which allows an administrator to place malicious code into their password which could then be dumped into a JSP file.

### Impact
#### Remote Code Execution (High severity)
This vulnerability can lead to executing arbitrary code if GeoServer is deployed in an environment where an attacker can dynamically deploy and execute a JSP file. This is possible if the geoserver.war file is simply placed into the webapps directory of a default Tomcat installation.

#### NTLM Hash Disclosure (Moderate severity)
If GeoServer is deployed in a Windows operating system and the GeoServer administrator does not already have access to the Windows account running the GeoServer process, it may be possible for the administrator to make GeoServer trigger an outbound NTLM request to a remote, attacker-controlled server and gain access to the NTLM hash or user password for use in future attacks.

#### Denial of Service (Low severity)
This vulnerability allows writing a file to any location where the GeoServer process has write permissions which could still potentially cause some kind of denial of service.

### Mitigation
GeoServer installations where the web interface is either disabled or completely removed are not affected since the vulnerability exists in one of the web pages.

### References
https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11852
https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/8584

summary: Denial-of-service (DoS)  Vulnerability in Jiffle process
description:
### Summary
Malicious Jiffle scripts can be executed by GeoServer, either as a rendering transformation in WMS dynamic styles or as a WPS process, that can enter an infinite loop to trigger denial of service.

### Details
The Jiffle language supports multiple loop constructs that will cause its code block to be continuously executed until a certain condition is met. The Jiffle runtime should be updated to throw an exception if the script exceeds a certain number of loop iterations.

### Impact
This vulnerability allows attackers to conduct denial-of-service attacks.

### Mitigation
This vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling WMS dynamic styling (see [WMS Settings](https://docs.geoserver.org/latest/en/user/services/wms/webadmin.html#disabling-usage-of-dynamic-styling-in-getmap-getfeatureinfo-and-getlegendgraphic-requests)).
If the WPS extension is installed, the Jiffle process must also be disabled to mitigate this vulnerability (see [WPS Settings](https://docs.geoserver.org/latest/en/user/services/wps/security.html#input-limits))

### References
https://github.com/geosolutions-it/jai-ext/pull/307
https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11778

summary: XML External Entity (XXE) Processing Vulnerability in GeoServer WFS Service
description:
## Summary

GeoServer Web Feature Service (WFS) web service was found to be vulnerable to GeoTools CVE-2025-30220 XML External Entity (XXE) processing attack.

It is possible to trigger the parsing of external DTDs and entities, bypassing standard entity resolvers.  This allows for Out-of-Band (OOB) data exfiltration of local files accessible by the GeoServer process, and Service Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

## Details

While direct entity resolution is managed by application property ENTITY_RESOLUTION_ALLOWLIST for XML Parsing, this restriction was not being used by the GeoTools library when building an in-memory XSD Library Schema representation.

This bypasses GeoServer's AllowListEntityResolver enabling XXE attacks.

## PoC

No public PoC is provided but this vulnerability has been confirmed to be exploitable through WFS service.

## Impact

* Information Disclosure: 

  This vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files from the server's filesystem that are accessible to the GeoServer process.
  
  This can lead to exposure of sensitive information including configuration files, credentials, and system files. The attack can be performed remotely without authentication, making it particularly severe.

* Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) 
  
  The mechanism inherently allows forcing GeoServer to make HTTP requests to arbitrary URLs, enabling SSRF attacks against internal network resources 

## References

* [CVE-2025-30220](https://github.com/geotools/geotools/security/advisories/GHSA-826p-4gcg-35vw) XML External Entity (XXE) Processing Vulnerability in XSD schema handling
* [External Entities Resolution](https://docs.geoserver.org/latest/en/user/production/config.html#production-config-external-entities) (GeoServer User Manual)

## Acknowledgements

This vulnerability was initially reported via an automated tool described below. Subsequently a duplicate report via @YacineF, and their patience working with the GeoServer project, was instrumental finding in escalating this issue and determining a resolution.

### XBOW-025-068 Disclaimer

This vulnerability was detected using **[XBOW](https://xbow.com/)**, a system that autonomously finds and exploits potential security vulnerabilities. The finding has been thoroughly reviewed and validated by a security researcher before submission. While XBOW is intended to work autonomously, during its development human experts ensure the accuracy and relevance of its reports.

summary: Unauthenticated XML External Entities (XXE) via WMS GetMap operation
description:
## Description

An XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability was identified. The application accepts XML input through a specific endpoint ``/geoserver/wms`` operation ``GetMap``. However, this input is not sufficiently sanitized or restricted, allowing an attacker to define external entities within the XML request.

An XML External Entity attack is a type of attack that occurs when XML input containing a reference to an external entity is processed by a weakly configured XML parser. This attack may lead to the disclosure of confidential data, denial of service, port scanning from the perspective of the machine where the parser is located, and other system impacts.

By exploiting this vulnerability, an attacker can:
- Read arbitrary files from the server's file system.
- Conduct Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) to interact with internal systems.
- Execute Denial of Service (DoS) attacks by exhausting resources.

## Resolution

Update to GeoServer 2.25.6, GeoServer 2.26.3, or GeoServer 2.27.0.

## Impact

The XXE vulnerability can be used to retrieve arbitrary files from the server's file system.

## Reference

* https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11682
* XBOW-024-081

## Disclaimer

This vulnerability was detected using **[XBOW](https://xbow.com/)**, a system that autonomously finds and exploits potential security vulnerabilities. The finding has been thoroughly reviewed and validated by a security researcher before submission. While XBOW is intended to work autonomously, during its development human experts ensure the accuracy and relevance of its reports.

summary: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) vulnerability in processing FreeMarker templates
description:
### Summary
A server-side template injection (SSTI) vulnerability exist that allows an authenticated administrator to upload FreeMarker templates containing malicious content that can execute OS commands and read from or write to arbitrary files on the server. These FreeMarker templates are used in a plain GeoServer instance (no extension or community modules) for WMS GetFeatureInfo HTML and JSON and WMS GetMap KML and GeoRSS output formats.

### Details
The org.geoserver.template.TemplateUtils.getSafeConfiguration() method attempts to block access to the class freemarker.template.utility.Execute but it is still possible to gain access to it and other sensitive functionality by chaining a specific sequence of method calls.

### Impact
This vulnerability can lead to executing arbitrary code and reading and writing arbitrary files.

### Resolution
GeoServer 2.27.0 addresses this vulnerability with several new application properties:

* ``GEOSERVER_FREEMARKER_BLOCK_LIST``
* ``GEOSERVER_FREEMARKER_ALLOW_LIST``
* ``GEOSERVER_FREEMARKER_API_EXPOSED``

These application properties default to restricting the objects template authors can access, and limit access to "getter" methods used to access object properties.

### References
- [Accessing Instance Methods](https://docs.geoserver.org/latest/en/user/tutorials/GetFeatureInfo/html.html#accessing-instance-methods)
- https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11645
- https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11777
- https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/8164

summary: Coverage REST API Server Side Request Forgery
description:
### Summary

The Coverage rest api `/workspaces/{workspaceName}/coveragestores/{storeName}/{method}.{format}` allow to upload file with a specified url (with {method} equals 'url') with no restrict.

### Details

The Coverage rest api `/workspaces/{workspaceName}/coveragestores/{storeName}/{method}.{format}` allow to upload file with a specified url (with {method} equals 'url'). But this url has not been check with [URL Checks feature](https://docs.geoserver.org/latest/en/user/security/urlchecks.html#url-checks).

For example, should add the code below to check fileURL:

```java
URLCheckers.confirm(fileURL)
```

The vulnerable code was [RESTUtils.java](https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/blob/main/src/rest/src/main/java/org/geoserver/rest/util/RESTUtils.java#L176)

### Impact

This vulnerability presents the opportunity for Server Side Request Forgery.

summary: Missing Authorization on REST API Index
description:
### Summary
It is possible to bypass the default REST API security and access the index page.

### Details
The REST API security handles `rest` and its subpaths but not `rest` with an extension (e.g., `rest.html`).

### Impact
The REST API index can disclose whether certain extensions are installed.

### Workaround
In `${GEOSERVER_DATA_DIR}/security/config.xml`, change the paths for the `rest` filter to `/rest.*,/rest/**` and change the paths for the `gwc` filter to `/gwc/rest.*,/gwc/rest/**` and restart GeoServer.

### References
https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11664  
https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11776  
https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/8170

summary: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability in XML entity resolution
description:
### Summary
A GeoServer that uses `ENTITY_RESOLUTION_ALLOWLIST` may allow attacker to perform unauthenticated Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

### Details
This vulnerability requires that GeoServer is set up to use a proxy base URL and the `ENTITY_RESOLUTION_ALLOWLIST` (default since 2.25.0):

### Impact
This vulnerability allows an attacker to cause GeoServer to make requests to an unintended location.

### Workaround
GeoServer installations are only affected by this vulnerability if they use a proxy base URL that does not contain a URL path or end with a slash (e.g., `https://somesite.org` instead of `https://somesite.org/` or `https://somesite.org/geoserver`). If the proxy base URL does not contain a path, adding a slash to the end of the URL will mitigate this vulnerability.

### References
https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11867
https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/8622

summary: Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in evaluating property name expressions
description:
### Summary
Multiple OGC request parameters allow Remote Code Execution (RCE) by unauthenticated users through specially crafted input against a default GeoServer installation due to unsafely evaluating property names as XPath expressions.

### Details
The GeoTools library API that GeoServer calls evaluates property/attribute names for feature types in a way that unsafely passes them to the commons-jxpath library which can execute arbitrary code when evaluating XPath expressions. This XPath evaluation is intended to be used only by complex feature types (i.e., Application Schema data stores) but is incorrectly being applied to simple feature types as well which makes this vulnerability apply to **ALL** GeoServer instances.

### PoC
No public PoC is provided but this vulnerability has been confirmed to be exploitable through WFS GetFeature, WFS GetPropertyValue, WMS GetMap, WMS GetFeatureInfo, WMS GetLegendGraphic and WPS Execute requests.

### Impact
This vulnerability can lead to executing arbitrary code.

### Workaround

A workaround exists by removing the `gt-complex-x.y.jar` file from the GeoServer where `x.y` is the GeoTools version (e.g., `gt-complex-31.1.jar` if running GeoServer 2.25.1). This will remove the vulnerable code from GeoServer but may break some GeoServer functionality or prevent GeoServer from deploying if the gt-complex module is needed by an extension you are using:

Mitigation for `geoserver.war` deploy:

1. Stop the application server
2. Unzip `geoserver.war` into a directory
3. Locate the file `WEB-INF/lib/gt-complex-x.y.jar` and remove
4. Zip the directory into a new `geoserver.war`
5. Restart the application server

Mitigation for GeoServer binary:

1. Stop Jetty
2. Locate the file `webapps/geoserver/WEB-INF/lib/gt-complex-x.y.jar` and remove
3. Restart Jetty

The following extensions and community modules are known to have a direct dependency on `gt-complex` jar and are not expected function properly without it. This is not comprehensive list and additional GeoServer functionality may be dependent on the availability of `gt-complex` jar:
* Extensions: Application Schema, Catalog Services for the Web, MongoDB Data Store
* Community Modules: Features-Templating, OGC API Modules, Smart Data Loader, SOLR Data Store

Mitigation available for prior releases patching three jars in your existing install:

1. Patched `gt-app-schema`, `gt-complex` and `gt-xsd-core` jars may be downloaded for GeoServer: [2.25.1](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.25.1/geoserver-2.25.1-patches.zip/download), [2.24.3](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.24.3/geoserver-2.24.3-patches.zip/download), [2.24.2](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.24.2/geoserver-2.24.2-patches.zip/download), [2.23.2](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.23.2/geoserver-2.23.2-patches.zip/download), [2.22.2](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.22.2/geoserver-2.22.2-patches.zip/download), [2.21.5](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.21.5/geoserver-2.21.5-patches.zip/download), [2.21.4](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.21.4/geoserver-2.21.4-patches.zip/download),[2.20.7](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.20.7/geoserver-2.20.7-patches.zip/download), [2.20.4](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.20.4/geoserver-2.20.4-patches.zip/download), [2.19.2](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.19.2/geoserver-2.19.2-patches.zip/download), [2.18.0](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.18.0/geoserver-2.18.0-patches.zip/download).
  
   As example the 2.25.1 page links to [geoserver-2.25.1-patches.zip](https://sourceforge.net/projects/geoserver/files/GeoServer/2.25.1/geoserver-2.25.1-patches.zip/download) download on source forge.

2. Unzip the `geoserver-x.y.z-patches.zip` which contains three jars that have been patched to configure `commons-jxpath` with an empty function list prior to use. These files are drop-in replacements with identical file names to those they are replacing.

3. Follow the instructions above to locate `WEB-INF/lib` folder and replace the existing `gt-app-schema`, `gt-complex` and `gt-xsd-core` jars with those supplied by the patch.

summary: GWC Home Page exposes sensitive server information
description:
### Summary
The GeoWebCache home page includes version and revision information about the software in use. This information is sensitive from a security point of view because it allows software used by the server to be easily identified.

### Details
org.geowebcache.GeoWebCacheDispatcher.handleFrontPage(HttpServletRequest, HttpServletResponse) has no check to hide potentially sensitive information from users except for a hidden system property to hide the storage locations that defaults to showing the locations.

### PoC
Just open http://localhost:8080/geoserver/gwc/

### Impact
In addition to exposing the version and revision information, the home page will expose the config file and storage locations which may expose the system's temp directory location and whether or not GeoServer is running in a Windows operating system. The approximate server start time and some basic GWC usage information is also exposed.

### References
https://osgeo-org.atlassian.net/browse/GEOS-11677
https://github.com/geoserver/geoserver/pull/8189
https://github.com/GeoWebCache/geowebcache/issues/1344
